recommendation: On an explicitly approved and reconciled live restart, wrap the V58 live poller's public candle fetcher with the already-tested CompletedCandleSnapshotCache. Do not change strategy logic, routes, entry thresholds, exits, sizing, leverage, stops, or the 15-second runtime cadence.
why_now: The retired observer recorded 10 public-L2 HTTP 429 degraded cycles in 213 polls. After applying completed-minute reuse only to the observer, its successor still recorded 2 public-L2 HTTP 429 cycles in 124 polls. The remaining aggregate request budget includes an unchanged live poller that requests eight completed-candle snapshots every configured 15-second poll even though completed one-minute bars do not change within the minute.

facts_used: REST requests share a per-IP aggregate weight limit of 1200 per minute.
L2 book info requests have weight 2.
Other documented info requests have base weight 20.
Candle snapshot responses add weight per 60 returned items.
WebSockets are recommended for lowest-latency real-time data.

observed_problem_or_opportunity.problem: The shared per-IP REST budget can be exhausted by repeated unchanged completed-candle reads, creating explicit observer gaps and potentially competing with live public-data reads.

alternatives_considered.tradeoff: preserves the exact current process but leaves repeated HTTP 429 evidence gaps and shared-IP contention unresolved
targets a weight-2 request class and can reduce exact-depth freshness while leaving the higher-weight repeated candle reads unchanged
aligns with the venue's latency guidance but is a larger stateful transport change and does not address candle snapshot weight

expected_upside: Reduce redundant high-weight candle REST calls by approximately 69 percent at the observed live cadence and 75 percent at the configured cadence after warmup, increasing shared-IP headroom without changing completed-bar strategy inputs.
main_risks_and_failure_modes: A same-minute upstream correction would not be seen until the next minute.
A restart creates an initial full-lookback request burst and must preserve adopted-position and owned-stop reconciliation.
The aggregate IP budget includes unknown external processes, so this change may reduce but not eliminate HTTP 429 responses.
A cache defect could freeze a response missing the just-completed bar; the implementation currently refuses to cache that condition.
Any strategy output drift under identical completed bars would falsify behavior preservation.
